title: Planet and moon classes as conditions of the finished body
status: the conditions of every class are its row of physics/data/planet_class_fit.json (GEN.1207: the best-fit classifier); a row here gives only the name, the phrase, the sentence and the basis of a class (GEN.1432: the phrase is what a body's page says after "It is"; the sentence is a class page's own words and holds no number, because the page lists the conditions from that file under it). Every number marked design is a planetGen default refitted by the class sweep, not a measured constant
reserve_note: Letters no class uses. Boss (6:26 PM EDT 2026-10-23): a letter is never retired without asking him, and free letters are kept for new designations that make more sense; use none of them for anything else. Q was retired by Boss (6:07 PM EDT 2026-10-30, GEN.1135): a class that was only an orbit; the swing of the starlight is the stored flux_variation and an At a glance flag. The old wet reducing E was retired by Boss (6:57 PM EDT 2026-10-30, GEN.1142; it was F with steam and got no body) and the letter E now names the deep-frozen world (7:06 PM EDT).

mass_earth.label: mass
mass_earth.note: the body's mass in Earth masses

ocean_fraction.label: water cover
ocean_fraction.note: share of the surface covered by water, liquid, or frozen

water_mass_fraction.label: water share of the body's mass
water_mass_fraction.note: water share of the whole body's mass

hydrosphere.label: water state
hydrosphere.note: the stored water state: dry, vapor, ice, ice-covered ocean, surface ocean, brine seep, hycean

flux_variation.label: variation of starlight over the orbit
flux_variation.note: peak-to-peak variation of the starlight the body receives, as a fraction

share_<gas>.label: <gas> share of the air
share_<gas>.note: a stored gas's partial pressure over the surface pressure (o2, co2, co, n2, ar, h2, h2o, ch4, h2s, so2)

o2_partial_pa.label: oxygen pressure
o2_partial_pa.note: the oxygen's partial pressure; the classes judge oxygen by pressure, not share (GEN.1321): 3 kPa, 16 kPa and 35.5 kPa are 3, 16 and 35 percent of an Earth atmosphere

co2_partial_pa.label: carbon dioxide pressure
co2_partial_pa.note: the carbon dioxide's partial pressure; the oxygen-water classes judge it by pressure, not share (GEN.1321): 1 kPa is 1 percent of an Earth atmosphere

reducing_share.label: methane and hydrogen share of the air
reducing_share.note: the methane and hydrogen shares together

roundness_ratio.label: roundness ratio
roundness_ratio.note: the mean radius over the radius at which the body's own weight beats the strength of its material; 1 or more is round (physics/roundness.py)

hottest_region_k.label: mean temperature of the hottest latitude band
hottest_region_k.note: the hottest of the seven annual-mean latitude bands (GEN.1108)

coldest_region_k.label: mean temperature of the coldest latitude band
coldest_region_k.note: the coldest of the seven annual-mean latitude bands

day_temperature_k.label: hottest day temperature
day_temperature_k.note: the hottest band's mean plus half its day and night swing

night_temperature_k.label: coldest night temperature
night_temperature_k.note: the coldest band's mean less half its swing

wet_bulb_c.label: wet-bulb temperature at the hottest day
wet_bulb_c.note: habitability.wet_bulb_c of the hottest day and the stored humidity

relative_humidity.label: relative humidity of the air
relative_humidity.note: the stored relative humidity of the surface air

groundwater_present.label: groundwater (1 when there is some)
groundwater_present.note: 1 when a body with no surface liquid holds reachable or deep groundwater

ammonia_water_mass_fraction.label: ammonia share of the water's mass
ammonia_water_mass_fraction.note: the ammonia over the water's mass

phase_<family>.label: liquid phase of the <family> family
phase_<family>.note: 1 where the family's liquid (water, methane-ethane, sulfuric acid, ammonia-water, dense CO2) is a liquid at the body's temperature and pressure (phase_gate)

rows.name: Gas dwarf
rows.phrase: a gas dwarf: mostly rock and metal under a thick hydrogen and helium envelope, with no surface to stand on
rows.sentence: A gas dwarf: lighter than the ice giants, mostly rock and metal under a thick hydrogen and helium envelope, with no surface to stand on.
rows.basis: design: 10 Earth masses, the lower edge of the ice giants' range; the sweep finds no better cut

rows.name: Ice giant
rows.phrase: an ice giant: a thick hydrogen and helium envelope over an interior of rock, metal, and the ices its disk gave it
rows.sentence: An ice giant: between a gas dwarf and a gas giant in mass, a thick hydrogen and helium envelope over rock, metal, and ices.
rows.basis: design: 35 Earth masses, the cut that misplaces fewest of the drawn ice and gas giants (15 percent; their mass ranges overlap from 30 to 60); the envelope share of GEN.428 replaces it at the cut-over

rows.name: Gas giant
rows.phrase: a gas giant, mostly hydrogen and helium
rows.sentence: A gas giant: the heaviest of the giants, mostly hydrogen and helium.
rows.basis: design: the rest of the giants

rows.name: Small airless world
rows.phrase: a small, round, airless world
rows.sentence: A small airless world: round (its own weight beats the strength of its material), light, and with no air.
rows.basis: design (Boss 8:41 PM EDT 2026-10-30): airless, round (the roundness ratio, which Asteroid bodies fail) and below 0.1 Earth masses; the water rule is dropped. 0.1 Earth masses is the planet minimum inside the snow line

rows.name: Airless super-Earth
rows.phrase: a large, airless rocky world
rows.sentence: A barren, rocky super-Earth with no air: heavier than the dead worlds of class C.
rows.basis: design: 1.5 Earth masses, the lower edge of a super-Earth

rows.name: Dead world
rows.phrase: an airless world of rock or ice
rows.sentence: A dead world: a solid body with no air, bare rock or ice at its surface, more massive than a small airless world and lighter than a super-Earth.
rows.basis: design: 10 Pa, the edge of an exosphere; 0.1 Earth masses and up (Boss 8:41 PM EDT 2026-10-30)

rows.name: Volcanic world
rows.phrase: a volcanic world whose air carries outgassed sulfur dioxide
rows.sentence: A volcanic world: air with a high share of sulfur dioxide, outgassed by active volcanism.
rows.basis: design: 3 percent sulfur dioxide, which no non-volcanic mixture reaches

rows.name: Gas dwarf
rows.phrase: a gas dwarf: mostly rock and metal under a thick hydrogen and helium envelope, with no surface to stand on
rows.sentence: A gas dwarf: a small world, lighter than the ice giants, with a deep hydrogen envelope over an interior of mostly rock and metal.
rows.basis: design stand-in (GEN.1142, registry CL1): 30 percent hydrogen and 10 Earth masses; the same T as the giant row, for the terrestrial-kind bodies whose envelope outweighs a thin air

rows.name: Hot dense world
rows.phrase: a hot world under a very thick, heavy air
rows.sentence: A hot world under a very thick air that is not hydrogen, usually mostly carbon dioxide, often with water vapor.
rows.basis: design stand-in (GEN.1142, registry CL2): 10 bar, 400 K and under 30 percent hydrogen; cooler thick-air bodies take the later rows by their own conditions

rows.name: High-gravity world
rows.phrase: a heavy world with air and strong gravity
rows.sentence: A world with air and strong surface gravity (a heavy super-Earth).
rows.basis: design stand-in (GEN.1136, registry GV1): 2 g, about 1.6 Earth radii of a rocky planet, just past the 1.5 Earth radii that [R0572] count as Earth-sized in the habitable zone; was 1.25 g (design), which took most of them

rows.name: Marginal thin-air world
rows.phrase: a mild world whose air is too thin in oxygen to breathe without a mask
rows.sentence: A marginal world, Earth-like in pressure and temperature but hard to breathe without a mask. Its oxygen is thin and it holds carbon dioxide, which at the high end is a poison of its own.
rows.basis: design stand-in (GEN.1142, registry CL3): Boss's 6:57 PM EDT 10-30 reading of L (Earth-like, high carbon dioxide, low oxygen, near-Earth temperature); the numbers are fitted, 0.5 g is unchanged

rows.name: Thin-air world
rows.phrase: a world with thin air and mild temperatures
rows.sentence: An adaptable world with a thin atmosphere: air too thin to breathe whatever its oxygen, and a mean surface from freezing to warm.
rows.basis: design stand-in (GEN.1142, registry CL4; GEN.1306, registry AW4): 3 kPa and 273.15 to 320 K; the cold part goes to P; no oxygen cap

rows.name: Deep-frozen world
rows.phrase: a deep-frozen world that still holds air
rows.sentence: A deep-frozen world: air and a mean surface far below freezing.
rows.basis: design stand-in (GEN.1142, registry CL7): -40 C, where Boss ended class P (the old wet reducing world E was retired, 6:57 PM EDT 10-30)

rows.name: Glaciated world
rows.phrase: a glaciated world, ice-covered except where the season melts it
rows.sentence: A glaciated world, the oxygen-water world too cold: a cool mean surface whose hottest region still melts in season, with poles that stay frozen.
rows.basis: design stand-in (GEN.1142, registry CL5, CL7): freezing (273.15 K) at the top, up from 210 K, and -40 C (233.15 K) at the bottom, below which a body is class E

rows.name: Frozen world
rows.phrase: a frozen world with air, below freezing but not deep-frozen
rows.sentence: A frozen world: an air world with a mean surface below freezing that is not Earth-like enough to be class P. Colder it is class E, the deep-frozen world.
rows.basis: design stand-in (GEN.1306, registry AW8): the gap between class P and class E, on the lines of E and P; Boss 11-06

rows.name: Small hot world
rows.phrase: a small world that holds on to air and stays above freezing
rows.sentence: A small world with air and a mean surface above freezing, with low surface gravity. It can be scorching, and some hold liquid water.
rows.basis: design: 0.5 g

rows.name: Anoxic world
rows.phrase: a world with air that has almost no free oxygen
rows.sentence: A world with an anoxic air (almost no free oxygen, and not mostly carbon dioxide), a surface above freezing that runs from cool to hot, and a gravity not far from Earth's.
rows.basis: design

rows.name: Carbon dioxide world
rows.phrase: a rocky world with a carbon dioxide air
rows.sentence: A rocky world with a carbon dioxide air (whatever the oxygen), a surface above freezing that runs from cool to hot (hotter and denser is class N), and neither light nor very heavy.
rows.basis: design

rows.name: Ocean world
rows.phrase: an ocean world, its surface mostly liquid water
rows.sentence: An ocean world, the oxygen-water world too wet: water covers most of the surface, at a mild mean surface temperature.
rows.basis: design stand-in (GEN.1142, registry CL6): 80 percent, from 90

rows.name: Desert world
rows.phrase: a desert world with little liquid water
rows.sentence: A desert world, the oxygen-water world too dry: some water but little of the surface, with groundwater below it, at a mild mean surface temperature.
rows.basis: design stand-in (GEN.1142, registry CL6): 20 percent, from 15

rows.name: Temperate world
rows.phrase: a temperate world with liquid water and breathable air
rows.sentence: A temperate world, the Earth-like sweet spot: a mild mean surface with liquid water over part of it, and an air with enough oxygen to breathe and little carbon dioxide.
rows.basis: design: the rest of the worlds with air

rows.name: Hothouse world
rows.phrase: a hothouse world too hot and wet for its air to cool
rows.sentence: A hothouse world, the oxygen-water world too hot and wet for its air to cool: a hot mean surface and a high wet-bulb temperature.
rows.basis: design (GEN.1221, Boss confirmed the letter at 11:59 AM EDT 2026-10-31); the conditions are its row of physics/data/planet_class_fit.json

rows.name: Hot thin-air world
rows.phrase: a hot world with thin air and no ocean
rows.sentence: A hot, thin-air world: a hot surface, thin air, no ocean, and gravity short of class V's.
rows.basis: design (GEN.1221, Boss confirmed the letter at 11:59 AM EDT 2026-10-31); the conditions are its row of physics/data/planet_class_fit.json

rows.name: Methane-ethane world
rows.phrase: a cold world with seas of liquid methane and ethane
rows.sentence: A cold world with seas of liquid methane and ethane under a thick air with methane in it.
rows.basis: design (GEN.1221, Boss confirmed the letter at 11:59 AM EDT 2026-10-31); the conditions are its row of physics/data/planet_class_fit.json

rows.name: Sulfuric acid world
rows.phrase: a sulfuric acid world, with liquid acid under a sulfur-rich air
rows.sentence: A sulfuric acid world: liquid sulfuric acid at the surface, under a sulfur-rich air.
rows.basis: design (GEN.1221, Boss confirmed the letter at 11:59 AM EDT 2026-10-31); the conditions are its row of physics/data/planet_class_fit.json

rows.name: Ammonia-water world
rows.phrase: an ammonia-water world, its ocean often under an ice lid
rows.sentence: An ammonia-water world: an ocean of ammonia and water, cold enough to stay liquid and often under an ice lid.
rows.basis: design (GEN.1221, Boss confirmed the letter at 11:59 AM EDT 2026-10-31); the conditions are its row of physics/data/planet_class_fit.json

core_note: Boss (6:30 PM EDT 2026-10-23): H, P, O, J, M, I, C, D and N are the core classes. Keep their letters and meanings as close to today's as the conditions allow.

asteroid.name: Asteroid
asteroid.phrase: an asteroid, a body too small for its own weight to pull it round
asteroid.sentence: An asteroid: a body whose own weight does not beat the strength of its material, so it is not round. It is an object type, not a planet class, has no class letter, and can be a moon.
asteroid.basis: Boss 8:41 PM EDT 2026-10-30 and 10:26 PM EDT: bodies under a roundness ratio of 1 are the object type Asteroid
